Which operator assigns a value to a PL/SQL variable?
Why is `l_name employees.last_name%TYPE;` preferred over hardcoding `VARCHAR2(25)`?

options.text: It anchors `l_name` to the column's data type and length automatically, surviving schema `ALTER TABLE` changes

questions.prompt: Select all valid parameter modes for PL/SQL procedures and functions. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: `IN OUT` (passes initial value in and returns updated value out)

questions.prompt: Match each PL/SQL anchor or scalar type to its purpose.

columns.label: Declares a variable with the same type as a table column or another variable
Declares a record matching all columns of a table or cursor row
Native hardware 32-bit signed integer faster than `NUMBER` for loop/integer math

questions.prompt: What happens in PL/SQL when `SELECT salary INTO l_sal FROM employees WHERE employee_id = 999;` finds zero rows?
What does `NVL(l_bonus, 0)` vs `COALESCE(a, b, 0)` do?

options.text: `NVL` takes 2 arguments; `COALESCE` takes 2+ arguments and short-circuits on the first non-NULL expression

questions.prompt: How do you test for `NULL` in PL/SQL `IF` conditions?
Which operator concatenates two strings in PL/SQL?
What does `q'[It's a test]'` (Oracle alternative quoting syntax) solve?

options.text: Allows single quotes `'` inside string literals without doubling `''`

questions.prompt: What is the key difference between a PL/SQL `PROCEDURE` and a `FUNCTION`?

options.text: A `FUNCTION` must return a value via `RETURN` and (when pure) can be called inside SQL queries; a `PROCEDURE` performs an action without returning a value directly

questions.prompt: How is `ELSIF` spelled in PL/SQL `IF` statements?

options.text: `ELSE IF` (single keyword? No, `ELSE IF` requires an extra `END IF`!)

questions.prompt: What does `FOR i IN REVERSE 1..5 LOOP` iterate over?
Select all true statements about `DBMS_OUTPUT.PUT_LINE` in Oracle. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Useful for quick debugging in dev, not a replacement for persistent logging tables
Writes directly to the OS console of end users' browsers
Buffers text lines for client tools (SQL*Plus, SQLcl, SQL Developer) to display after execution
Requires `SET SERVEROUTPUT ON` in SQL*Plus/SQLcl to print output

questions.prompt: What does `EXIT WHEN l_idx > 10;` do inside a basic `LOOP ... END LOOP;`?

options.text: Exits the loop immediately when `l_idx > 10` is true (like `break`)

questions.prompt: What does `c_pi CONSTANT NUMBER := 3.14159;` enforce?

options.text: `c_pi` must be initialized at declaration and cannot be reassigned

questions.prompt: What does `ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT sp_before_step2;` do?

options.text: Undoes DML changes made *after* `sp_before_step2` while keeping earlier transaction work intact

questions.prompt: What does `CASE l_grade WHEN 'A' THEN 'Excellent' ELSE 'Other' END` demonstrate?

options.text: A searched or simple `CASE` expression returning a value

questions.prompt: What does `/` on its own line after `END;` do in SQL*Plus / SQLcl / SQL Developer?

options.text: Executes the PL/SQL block currently in the SQL buffer

questions.prompt: Match each PL/SQL transaction or DML keyword to its effect.

columns.label: Makes all DML changes in the current transaction permanent and releases row locks
Undoes all uncommitted DML changes in the current transaction
Captures generated column values (e.g., sequence/identity PK) from `INSERT`/`UPDATE`/`DELETE` without an extra `SELECT`

questions.prompt: Why should `COMMIT` and `ROLLBACK` usually be controlled by the caller/top-level orchestrator rather than buried inside low-level helper procedures?

options.text: Embedding `COMMIT` inside helpers breaks transaction atomicity across multi-step workflows and makes rollback impossible on later failures

questions.prompt: What is the `BOOLEAN` data type's behavior in classic PL/SQL vs SQL (pre-Oracle 23ai)?

options.text: PL/SQL has native `BOOLEAN` (`TRUE`, `FALSE`, `NULL`), whereas pre-23ai Oracle SQL tables didn't have a native `BOOLEAN` column type

questions.prompt: What does `SQL%ROWCOUNT` return immediately after an `UPDATE` statement in PL/SQL?

options.text: The number of rows modified by that most recent implicit SQL statement

code.source:
UPDATE accounts SET active = 'N' WHERE id = l_id;
IF SQL%ROWCOUNT = 0 THEN RAISE NO_DATA_FOUND; END IF;

questions.prompt: What does `CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE` do if the procedure already exists?

options.text: Replaces the procedure definition while preserving existing `GRANT`ed privileges on it

questions.prompt: Select all valid comment syntaxes in PL/SQL. (Select all that apply.)
What does `l_row employees%ROWTYPE;` declare?

options.text: A composite record with one field for every column in `employees`

questions.prompt: What does `CONTINUE WHEN MOD(i, 2) = 0;` do inside a `FOR` loop?

options.text: Skips the rest of the current iteration when `i` is even and proceeds to the next `i`

questions.prompt: What does `VARCHAR2(100 CHAR)` vs `VARCHAR2(100 BYTE)` specify?

options.text: `100 CHAR` reserves up to 100 Unicode characters regardless of UTF-8 byte length; `100 BYTE` caps at 100 bytes

questions.prompt: What does `SUBSTR('Oracle', 1, 3)` return in PL/SQL?
What does `SHOW ERRORS` in SQL*Plus / SQLcl display after `Warning: Procedure created with compilation errors`?

options.text: The compiler line/column error messages from `USER_ERRORS`

questions.prompt: What does `SYSDATE` vs `SYSTIMESTAMP` return?

options.text: `SYSDATE` returns `DATE` (second precision, no fractional seconds/tz); `SYSTIMESTAMP` returns `TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE` (fractional seconds + TZ)

questions.prompt: What does `l_count PLS_INTEGER NOT NULL := 0;` enforce?

options.text: Requires initialization at declaration and raises `VALUE_ERROR` if `NULL` is ever assigned

questions.prompt: Match each PL/SQL conditional or loop keyword to its closing keyword.
What happens if a `FUNCTION` finishes its body without executing a `RETURN` statement?

options.text: Raises `ORA-06503: PL/SQL: Function returned without value` at runtime

questions.prompt: What does `named notation` (`create_user(p_email => 'a@b.com', p_role => 'admin')`) improve?

options.text: Readability and safety against parameter-order mistakes, plus skipping optional `DEFAULT` parameters

questions.prompt: What does `TO_DATE('2026-11-20', 'YYYY-MM-DD')` do?

options.text: Parses a string into an Oracle `DATE` using the explicit format mask (never rely on implicit `NLS_DATE_FORMAT`!)

questions.prompt: Select all true statements about nested PL/SQL blocks (`BEGIN ... BEGIN ... EXCEPTION ... END; ... END;`). (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Inner blocks can declare local variables and their own `EXCEPTION` handlers
If an inner block catches an exception, execution continues in the enclosing outer block after the inner `END;`
Labels like `<<outer>>` let you qualify shadowed variable names (`outer.l_x`)
Nested blocks run in separate database sessions

questions.prompt: What does `<<outer_loop>>` label before a loop allow?

options.text: Exiting or continuing an outer loop directly from inside an inner nested loop (`EXIT outer_loop;`)

questions.prompt: What does `NUMBER(10, 2)` declare?

options.text: Up to 10 total significant digits, with 2 digits to the right of the decimal point

questions.prompt: What does `MERGE INTO target ... WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE ... WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT` do?

options.text: Performs an atomic 'upsert' (update if exists, insert if not) in a single SQL statement

questions.prompt: Select all true statements about `DROP PROCEDURE` vs `CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE`. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: `CREATE OR REPLACE` deletes all rows from tables used by the procedure
`CREATE OR REPLACE` keeps existing object privileges (`GRANT`s)
`DROP PROCEDURE` revokes/removes all privileges granted on that procedure
Invalidated dependent packages automatically recompile on next valid call (or via `ALTER ... COMPILE`)

questions.prompt: What does `l_str := NULL;` followed by `LENGTH(l_str)` return in Oracle PL/SQL?

options.text: `NULL` (because in Oracle `''` empty string and `NULL` are treated identically for `VARCHAR2`!)
